newsitem.title: TAIWAN: CPC to try crude offload at repaired Taiwan port.
newsitem.headline: CPC to try crude offload at repaired Taiwan port.

text.p: State-owned Chinese Petroleum has repaired its northern Taiwan crude offloading units and plans to start pumping 550,000 tonnes of crude from two tankers on Thursday, company officials said.
"A team of engineers is at the Taoyuan offshore crude port to start offloading two crude tankers waiting in nearby waters," a Chinese Petroleum official told Reuters by telephone.
Engineers hoped to begin the unloading on Thursday afternoon, he said.
The port was first shut down on September 15 due to unspecified pipeline problems, shutting off the flow of crude to Chinese Petroleum's adjacent refinery at Taoyuan.
Rough seas caused by a series of typhoons have thwarted repairs, keeping the port closed since mid-September with the exception of a brief period on September 25.
The official said two crude tankers, the 250,000-tonne Felipe Camarao and 300,000-tonne Vanadis, were waiting to offload cargoes badly needed by the refinery.
Crude supplies remained tight at the refinery despite the successful offloading of 200,000 tonnes of crude from the tanker Arcadian during the brief reopening on September 25.
Refinery officials earlier had said the 200,000 tonnes had been pumped from the Vanadis.
The Arcadian discharged its remaining 100,000 tonnes of African crude at Chinese Petroleum's southern port at Kaohsiung, company officials said.
The unlucky tanker Vanadis, which arrived at Taoyuan around September 15, has been forced to wait for 16 days to unload its 300,000 tonne cargo.
Industry sources told Reuters the Vanadis was being compensated at a rate of US$30,000 a day for the delay. Chinese Petroleum declined to comment on the reported compensation.
Low crude supplies forced Chinese Petroleum to shut one of the Taoyuan refinery's two 100,000-barrel-per-day distillation or topping units to slow its crude consumption.
The Taoyuan refinery's main product is jet oil, turning out 60,000 tonnes a month at full capacity. It is the principal supplier to Taipei's busy international airport at Taoyuan.
The slowed production forced Chinese Petroleum to increase its purchases jet oil in the Asian energy market.
Chinese Petroleum has bought two 32,000-tonne shipments of jet fuel since the refinery's cut production and issued another tender on Tuesday for one more shipment.
